senses.gloss:
Ṭaṅka
or Brahmanandin, also called Ātreya an. Vākyakāra; ref. to by Rāmānuja in his Vedārthasaṅgraha; by Yāmunācārya in Ātmasiddhi etc.
--C. Vākya on Chāndogyopaniṣad. See under C.. up.
See V. Krishnamacharya, ‘Ṭaṅka an. Dramiḍa’ Āchārya Dhruva Smāraka Grantha III. p.. 222-5; Hiriyanna, ‘Fragments from Brahmanandin’, K. B. Pathak Commemoration Volume p.. 151-58; Van Buitenen, Intro. to his edn. of Vedārthasaṅgraha, p.. 24-29.
For a. attempt to take him a. a. Advaitin see Polakam Rama Sastrin, Drāviḍātreyadarśanam, Madras.

Ṭaṅkaṇa
authority consulted by a. of Ratnākarauṣadhayogagrantha, MD. 13190.

Ṭaṅkadāsa
or Ḍam3gadāsa of Bengal; described a. a Vṛddhakāyastha an. contemporary of Dharmapāla of Bengal.
--C. Suviśadasam3puṭa on Hevajratantra; written a. the Pāṇḍubhūmivihāra. Cordier II. p. 57.
See NIA. I. p. 12.

Ṭaṅkācārya
Q. by Ham3sayogin in Gītābhāṣya. See F. O. Schrader, Festgabe Garbe p. 179. Identity with ancient Ṭaṅka doubtful.
See Van Buitenen, op. cit. p. 27. [Page001-b]

Ṭaṅkipāda
or Lūhipāda.
--Buddhodaya. Bud. Cordier III. p. 116.
